title: 7 Adobe-style apps rebuilt with AI, and the tool that helps agents understand apps
repository_description: One MCP for reverse engineering across binaries, applications, and runtime behavior.

verified_features.label: Seven Adobe-style open-source apps
verified_features.claim: ArtCraft publishes seven open-source apps, each described as a clean-room reimplementation of an Adobe app: PhotoCraft (Photoshop), FilmCraft (Premiere Pro), VectorCraft (Illustrator), EffectCraft (After Effects), LightCraft (Lightroom), DesignCraft (InDesign), PdfCraft (Acrobat).
verified_features.evidence: README taglines of github.com/storytold/{photocraft,filmcraft,vectorcraft,effectcraft,lightcraft,designcraft,printcraft} at the commits in verification.artcraft_commits; screenshots are the repos' own docs/images (MIT OR Apache-2.0 per NOTICE / ATTRIBUTION.md)

verified_features.label: Built with AI help (developer's statement)
verified_features.claim: The developer told reporters he used Anthropic's Claude to write the apps; every repo ships AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md guides for AI agents.
verified_features.evidence: PetaPixel 2026-10-07, Notebookcheck, TechRepublic (verification.sources); AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in each repo. The repos' READMEs themselves do not state how much was AI-written, so the hook keeps a question mark.

verified_features.label: Plugs into AI coding agents over MCP
verified_features.claim: REA runs as an MCP server that AI coding agents call.
verified_features.evidence: rea --mcp answered initialize + tools/list with 207 tools; an agent then called capture_process_scenario and inspect_with_objdump through it (transcript-trimmed.jsonl). README: setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI.

verified_features.label: Works without the source code
verified_features.claim: REA inspected a stripped binary whose source had been deleted before the investigation.
verified_features.evidence: mystery-filter sha256 fa577326…632c, ELF stripped; source removed before the agent started; disasm-main-loop.txt is REA's inspect_with_objdump output

verified_features.label: Observes what an app does
verified_features.claim: capture_process_scenario ran the app and recorded its output and exit.
verified_features.evidence: capture evidence: exit code 0, terminal output 'filtered 600x600 (13600 px locked)' (transcript-trimmed.jsonl, call 1)

verified_features.label: Inspects compiled code
verified_features.claim: inspect_with_objdump returned the disassembly the agent read the filter's rules from.
verified_features.evidence: disasm-main-loop.txt lines 0x1290–0x1334; findings.md cites each address

verified_features.label: Traces behaviour
verified_features.claim: REA has commands that trace a feature through analysed references and captured behaviour.
verified_features.evidence: rea --help: trace, trace-application-feature, trace-javascript-semantics, capture-process (rea-agents 6.5.0). This episode ran capture_process_scenario, not the trace commands.

verified_features.label: Helps recreate a specific feature
verified_features.claim: From REA's evidence the agent rewrote the filter; its output matched the original byte for byte.
verified_features.evidence: rebuild.py; cmp original-out.ppm rebuilt-out.ppm: 0 of 1,080,015 bytes differ (both sha256 71d30378…c74c1f)

verified_features.label: Not a one-click cloner
verified_features.claim: REA is an investigation tool; the project does not support copying proprietary software.
verified_features.evidence: DISCLAIMER.md (Responsible use): 'does not support … copying proprietary software or reproducing its protected code and assets'

demonstration.meaning: a real screen/webcam capture of the project running
notes: Shock / context / mystery beats show ArtCraft's own published screenshots (MIT OR Apache-2.0; artwork in them is public domain), labelled as open-source recreations, not Adobe.

Proof / possibility beats show a real REA 6.5.0 investigation captured for this episode: a separate AI agent with only a stripped test binary called REA over MCP and rebuilt the filter; outputs compared byte for byte.
The test app was written by the DevMimo pipeline for this demo (its source was deleted before the investigation); it is not third-party software.
REA was not used on ArtCraft or on any Adobe product.

verification.environment: Ubuntu 24.04 container, Node 22.22.0, GNU objdump; no Hopper / Ghidra / IDA
verification.run: REA's MCP stdio server (rea --mcp) driven over JSON-RPC by a separate AI agent that had only a stripped binary; evidence in series/mimo-found-this-on-github/evidence/episode-002-rea/
verification.relationship: ArtCraft (github.com/storytold) and REA (github.com/morluto/rea) are separate projects by different people. ArtCraft describes its apps as clean-room reimplementations; nothing says REA was used to build them. The reel presents them as two separate discoveries.
sources: https://github.com/storytold/photocraft and the six sibling repositories (README taglines, NOTICE, ATTRIBUTION.md)

source_references: https://github.com/storytold/photocraft and the six sibling repositories (README taglines, NOTICE, ATTRIBUTION.md)

narration_script.shock: Someone recreated seven Adobe-style apps using AI.
narration_script.context: Photoshop. Premiere. Illustrator. Even After Effects.
narration_script.mystery: And people are rebuilding more software every day.
narration_script.discovery: I found a GitHub project called Reverse Engineer Anything.
narration_script.proof: Connect it to an AI coding agent, and it can investigate how software works, even without the original source code.
narration_script.possibility: It can inspect code, trace behavior, and help recreate specific features.
narration_script.question: But imagine what you could build. What app would you reverse engineer?

instagram_caption:
Someone recreated seven Adobe-style apps using AI. 👀

And there's a GitHub project that helps AI agents investigate how software actually works.

Meet REA — Reverse Engineer Anything.

Not a magic app cloner. But a fascinating tool for understanding and rebuilding software behavior.

(The seven apps are ArtCraft's open-source projects, a separate project. In the Reel, an AI agent used REA on a small test app we built, without its source, and rebuilt one feature exactly.)

👾 Mimo Found This on GitHub — EP. 002
